chunks: He left behind a son named al-Hasan, known by the kunya Abu Ali and nicknamed al-Mufid al-Thani (the Second Mufid), among the most renowned scholars.
He succeeded his father in teaching and issuing legal opinions (fatawa). He passed away in the year 515 AH, and he left behind great works.

key_terms.آثَارٌ جَلِيلَةٌ: great works — a formulaic phrase in biographical literature denoting scholarly writings of lasting significance
key_terms.الْفَتْيَا: issuing fatawa — the authoritative function of a senior jurist in answering legal questions for the community
key_terms.الْمُفِيدِ الثَّانِي: al-Mufid al-Thani — 'the Second Mufid', a title connecting him to the tradition of Shaykh al-Mufid, his father's own teacher

ai.seo_question: Who was al-Mufid al-Thani, the son of Shaykh al-Tusi, and what was his contribution to Shia scholarship?
ai.summary: This biographical note records that Shaykh al-Ta'ifa (al-Tusi, d. 460 AH) left behind a son, al-Hasan, titled al-Mufid al-Thani, who became one of the most distinguished Shia scholars of his era. He faithfully carried on his father's dual role as teacher and jurist until his death in 515 AH, and his scholarly legacy endured through his major written works.
word_analysis: he is known by the kunya
